raw.excerpt: About Bask HealthBask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
raw.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a UX Researcher, Patient & Provider Experience to help Bask Health better understand how patients and healthcare professionals interact with digital healthcare experiences.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools.

As a UX Researcher, Patient & Provider Experience, you'll investigate how people navigate healthcare-related interfaces, complete important tasks, interpret information, and interact with workflows that may involve sensitive or complex information.

This is a hands-on research role focused on evaluating patient and provider experiences through user interviews, usability testing, workflow observation, and qualitative analysis.

Your research will help product teams identify where users encounter confusion, unnecessary complexity, or barriers to completing tasks.

On the patient side, you'll study experiences such as onboarding, intake questionnaires, form completion, account interactions, and the communication of next steps.

You'll investigate whether patients understand the information being requested, can navigate multi-step workflows, and know what to expect after completing an action.

On the provider side, you'll study relevant clinical interfaces and operational workflows, including how authorized healthcare professionals review information, navigate tasks, and interact with the platform.

You'll pay particular attention to how information moves between patient-facing and provider-facing experiences, identifying usability issues that may affect clarity, efficiency, or workflow continuity.

You'll work closely with product designers to evaluate prototypes, test interaction patterns, and improve the organization and presentation of information.

You'll collaborate with product managers to define research questions and prioritize studies that address important product decisions.

You'll partner with engineers to understand technical constraints and ensure findings can be translated into practical improvements.

You'll also collaborate with appropriate clinical and operational stakeholders to understand workflow requirements and ensure research activities respect professional responsibilities and healthcare-related boundaries.

Because these experiences may involve sensitive information, you'll conduct research with careful attention to participant privacy, informed consent, approved research environments, and appropriate data-handling procedures.

You'll evaluate accessibility, comprehension, and the needs of users with different levels of technical familiarity or healthcare knowledge.

You'll synthesize research findings into actionable recommendations that help teams improve usability while preserving the accuracy and intent of healthcare-related workflows.

We're looking for someone who is curious about how people interact with healthcare software, comfortable researching complex user journeys, and able to translate detailed observations into meaningful product improvements.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct UX research across Bask Health's patient-facing and provider-facing software experiences.
  • Plan and execute usability studies involving healthcare-related digital workflows.
  • Conduct interviews with patients and authorized healthcare professionals through approved research processes.
  • Evaluate patient onboarding and account creation experiences.
  • Study the usability of digital intake questionnaires and multi-step forms.
  • Research how patients understand questions, instructions, and required information.
  • Identify friction points affecting patient task completion.
  • Evaluate patient navigation, information architecture, and interface comprehension.
  • Test prototypes for patient-facing features before development.
  • Study relevant provider interfaces and clinical workflow interactions.
  • Research how authorized providers navigate and review information within the platform.
  • Evaluate task organization, information presentation, and workflow efficiency.
  • Identify usability challenges involving patient-to-provider workflow transitions.
  • Collaborate with clinical and operational stakeholders to understand relevant workflow requirements.
  • Develop research plans, interview guides, and usability testing materials.
  • Recruit and screen appropriate research participants through approved processes.
  • Conduct moderated and unmoderated usability studies where appropriate.
  • Observe user behavior and identify recurring usability patterns.
  • Evaluate task completion, navigation difficulties, and user errors.
  • Collaborate with product designers to validate proposed interaction improvements.
  • Partner with content designers to evaluate healthcare terminology and user comprehension.
  • Work with product managers to prioritize patient and provider research opportunities.
  • Incorporate available behavioral data and user feedback into research findings.
  • Apply accessibility and inclusive research principles to study design.
  • Follow appropriate privacy, consent, and sensitive-data handling procedures.
  • Develop research reports and actionable design recommendations.
  • Present findings to product, design, engineering, and relevant operational teams.
  • Maintain organized research documentation and reusable insights.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in UX research, user research, human-computer interaction, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or case studies demonstrating UX research for digital products.
  • Experience independently planning and conducting usability studies.
  • Strong understanding of qualitative research methods.
  • Experience conducting moderated user interviews.
  • Familiarity with unmoderated usability testing.
  • Ability to develop clear research questions and study objectives.
  • Experience creating usability tasks, interview guides, and research materials.
  • Understanding of user-centered design principles.
  • Ability to evaluate complex digital workflows and user journeys.
  • Experience identifying usability problems and recommending improvements.
  • Familiarity with task-based usability evaluation.
  • Experience analyzing qualitative findings and identifying recurring patterns.
  • Ability to synthesize research findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Experience collaborating with product designers and product managers.
  • Familiarity with prototypes, wireframes, and iterative product development.
  • Understanding of accessibility and inclusive research practices.
  • Experience researching interfaces involving complex or sensitive information.
  • Familiarity with participant recruitment and screening.
  • Understanding of research ethics and informed consent.
  • Ability to communicate research findings to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Experience maintaining organized research documentation.
  • Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to independently manage research projects in a cross-functional environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience conducting UX research for healthcare or telehealth products.
  • Familiarity with patient-facing digital healthcare experiences.
  • Experience evaluating patient onboarding or intake questionnaires.
  • Understanding of health literacy and patient comprehension challenges.
  • Experience researching software used by clinicians or healthcare professionals.
  • Familiarity with clinical workflow interfaces.
  • Understanding of healthcare-related operational processes.
  • Experience working with clinicians, pharmacists, or healthcare operations teams.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA and healthcare-related privacy considerations.
  • Experience conducting research involving sensitive user information.
  • Understanding of accessibility standards such as WCAG.
  • Experience evaluating complex forms and conditional workflows.
  • Familiarity with tools such as UserTesting, Maze, Dovetail, Lookback, or comparable research platforms.
  • Experience evaluating Figma prototypes.
  • Familiarity with task-completion metrics and usability measurement.
  • Experience combining qualitative research with product analytics.
  • Understanding of information architecture testing methods.
  • Experience researching experiences involving multiple user roles or permissions.
  • Familiarity with white-label or configurable SaaS platforms.
  • Experience working in fast-moving, cross-functional product teams.

raw.description:
Founded in 2020, Lavender is the largest nurse-owned and operated online psychiatry and therapy office in the United States. Our extraordinary team of 100+ talented and like-minded folks works remotely from across the United States, Canada and the Philippines to collaboratively increase access to high-quality, high-touch mental healthcare. Lavender is a human-first organization and our people embody:

  • A bias towards action
  • A capacity for self-direction
  • Originality and creative instincts
  • Courageous and bold thinking
  • And the potential to achieve even more

If you’re looking for a fast-paced, constantly evolving environment where your voice matters and you can truly have an impact creating high-quality, user-centric mental health services, we want to hear from you!

Lavender is an equal opportunity employer. We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. We strongly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives and background will lead to a better environment for our team and a better experience for our clients. We strongly encourage people of color and members of the LGBTQ+ community to apply.

Join the Lavender team

We are looking for a Finance Operations Specialist to keep Lavender's finances running smoothly behind the scenes: ensuring vendors and partners are paid accurately and on time, keeping cash where each of our entities needs it, and maintaining clear, simple programs that let our teams spend responsibly on their own. You'll start with well-documented procedures so you can hit the ground running quickly—and from there, they're yours to improve, automate, and keep current.

The Opportunity

Reporting to and working closely with our Director of Finance, our accounting team, and leaders across the company, this is a part-time employee role (16–20 hours per week) based remotely in Canada. We're a growing healthcare company with several entities and clients across many US states, so no two weeks look the same. We're looking for someone who notices a gap next to their work and closes it—whether that's a filing deadline without an owner, a recurring travel question, or a spend report a director needs by Friday—with room to grow into cash forecasting and budget tracking as we scale.

Role Details:

  • Employment Type: Part-time Employee (approximately 16–20 hours per week)
  • Location: Remote, based in Canada (with some availability during Eastern Time business hours on payment days)
  • Compensation: $35.00 CAD per hour
  • Target Start Date: Early December 2026

What You'll be Doing

Payments and Vendor Management
  • Own the weekly vendor payment run from start to finish: review incoming bills, prepare payments, route them for approval, and release them on schedule.
  • Pay US and Canadian vendors and partners in USD and CAD across our banking and payment platforms.
  • Keep vendor records complete and current, including W-9s, contracts, payment details, and renewal dates.
  • Protect company funds by following our approval process, confirming any change to a vendor's bank details by phone before approval, and flagging anything that doesn't look right.
  • Serve as our first line of defence against fraud and waste—questioning requests that don't add up, investigating before money moves, and never sending funds just because someone asked.
  • Manage the shared finance inbox so questions get answered and nothing is missed.
  • Own year-end 1099 reporting: collect W-9s throughout the year, track which payees reach reporting thresholds, apply rules and exemptions correctly (for incorporated payees, attorneys, medical providers, and rent), and file on time.
Cash and Month-End Support
  • Prepare the weekly cash snapshot across our entities and the transfers that keep each one funded for approval.
  • Maintain a rolling 13-week cash forecast of payments and transfers built from our payment schedule.
  • Support month-end close with our external accounting team by answering transaction questions and gathering documentation.
  • Reconcile card and bill activity so every charge has an owner, a receipt, and the right code.
Travel and Expense Programs
  • Run our company card and expense program: issue and adjust cards, set limits, keep receipts and approvals on track, and help team members use it smoothly.
  • Manage our travel program (including Navan for booking and Uber for Business for ground transport) with clear guardrails so booking is self-serve.
  • Coordinate travel and spend for company events like our annual summit so 100+ travellers can book within budget.
  • Own our credit card and travel policies—reviewing them each year, improving the programs, and supporting and training the people who use them.
Compliance, Filings, and Insurance
  • Maintain a tax and compliance calendar so every filing and payment has a clear date and owner.
  • Prepare and submit recurring state and local filings (such as monthly Washington excise tax), annual entity filings, and information returns.
  • Set up tax and registration accounts as new entities go live.
  • Support annual insurance renewals (including commercial and malpractice) by gathering information, completing applications, and tracking deadlines.
  • Monitor recurring payments run by other teams (such as client referral rewards) against budget and escalate anything over set limits.
Spend Reporting and Process Improvement
  • Answer "how much did we spend on X?" questions for leaders using data from our spend management and accounting systems.
  • Help department heads track spend against their budgets as we introduce department budgets in 2027, flagging anything trending over budget.
  • Keep procedures current by documenting changes, automating manual steps, and ensuring someone else could step in seamlessly.
  • Proactively look for ways to improve processes and reduce costs, bringing recommendations backed by the numbers.

What You Bring

  • Experience: 4+ years in accounts payable, bookkeeping, or finance operations, ideally at a growing company with more than one legal entity.
  • Payments & Controls: Experience owning payments end-to-end across multiple bank and payment platforms, with strong instincts for internal controls, fraud prevention, and sound judgment around confidential financial information.
  • Tools & Systems: Working knowledge of QuickBooks Online and a modern spend management tool, plus comfort working remotely and asynchronously in Slack, Google Workspace, and Asana.
  • US Tax & Filing Knowledge: Hands-on experience preparing and filing 1099s (1099-NEC and 1099-MISC), including reporting thresholds, rules, and exemptions, plus familiarity with recurring US state or local filings.
  • Communication & Mindset: A self-starter who learns from documentation, asks good questions early, writes clearly and concisely, and can "hold a line kindly"—pointing people to policies and self-serve options while still leaving them feeling helped.
  • Work Setup: A quiet, professional space to work from home (company equipment and onboarding provided).
  • Preferred Qualifications: Experience paying vendors in both USD and CAD; running a travel program (Navan, TravelPerk, or Uber for Business); US healthcare, professional services, or multi-state company experience; and comfort building simple forecasts and models in Google Sheets or Excel.

Why You Should Join Lavender

  • Work for a company that is truly making a difference in the world
  • Remote work
  • A caring, spirited, and experienced team
  • An international work environment that embraces diversity and inclusion
  • Be part of a growing startup where you have the opportunity to help shape the company
  • In-person meetups
  • Competitive compensation ($28.00-$35.00 CAD/hour)
Bring your whole self to work

Lavender believes that nurturing an environment where diversity and inclusion can thrive is critical to our success. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of any status protected by law, including race, colour, religion, sex, orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, or genetic information.

About WCG

WCG delivers transformational solutions that accelerate clinical research and advance human health. We serve the experts, innovators, and pathfinders on the frontlines of science and medicine—empowering them to develop breakthrough therapies while ensuring the risks of progress never outweigh the value of human life. Together, we stimulate growth, maximize efficiency, and shape the future of clinical trials.

Why WCG

At WCG, we invest in our people because you are the driving force behind our mission. When you grow, our impact grows. When you thrive, research accelerates. We empower you to build a meaningful career while advancing the work that improves lives.

What we offer:

Comprehensive health and financial protection – Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, and flexible spending accountsResources that support your whole life – Employee assistance programs and work/life balance toolsInvestment in your growth – Referral bonuses, tuition reimbursement, on-the-job training, certification assistance, and continuing education supportTime to recharge – Paid holidays, vacation, and sick timePathways forward – Career development opportunities across One WCG

We practice transparency in everything we do, including compensation. The salary range for this position reflects our commitment to fair, competitive pay based on your qualifications, experience, skills, education, and location. Together, we'll find the right fit for your expertise and our shared mission.

Job Summary

The Senior Principal Statistical Programmer serves as a senior technical leader and subject matter expert in statistical programming, with deep expertise supporting clinical trials and Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) deliverables. This role combines advanced hands-on programming capabilities with technical leadership, driving the design, development, and standardization of high-quality statistical outputs. The Senior Principal Statistical Programmer independently leads complex programming initiatives, provides expert-level guidance across projects, and plays a key role in shaping programming standards, tools, and best practices. This role partners closely with biostatistics, project management, data management and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure high-quality, compliant, and efficient delivery of programming outputs.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily. The accountabilities listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required.

  • Serve as a senior technical expert in statistical programming, providing guidance across multiple studies or functional areas.
  • Design, develop, validate, and oversee complex statistical programming deliverables, including analysis datasets, tables, listings, and figures.
  • Lead the development, validation, and continuous improvement of DMC macros and programming standards.
  • Provide technical oversight and review of programming work to ensure quality, compliance, and consistency across deliverables.
  • Drive the establishment and adoption of programming standards, best practices, and process improvements.
  • Collaborate with biostatistics and study teams to support complex trial designs, analyses, and DMC reporting.
  • Independently manage and prioritize programming activities across multiple studies or initiatives.
  • Mentor and provide technical leadership to statistical programming staff, supporting skill development and best practices.
  • Contribute technical expertise to proposals, project planning, and scope discussions as needed.
  • Partner with IT and technology teams to support SAS environments, tools, and system validation efforts.
  • Provide technical oversight for programming activities supporting regulatory submissions and inspection readiness.
  • Ensure programming deliverables align with regulatory expectations, submission requirements, and CDISC standards.
  • Influence programming approaches, standards, and best practices across multiple studies or programs.
  • Serve as a technical escalation point for complex programming, data, or deliverable issues, leading resolution of highly complex or ambiguous challenges.
  • Provide expert interpretation of statistical analysis plans (SAPs), protocols, and study documents, translating requirements into programming strategy.
  • Champion process improvements, automation, and innovative approaches to enhance efficiency, scalability, and consistency of programming deliverables.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor. These may, on occasion, be unrelated to the position described here.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS: Master’s degree required. In limited circumstances, an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant professional experience may be considered.

QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum 8–10 years of statistical programming experience in a clinical trial environment.
  • Deep expertise in SAS programming, including complex analyses and regulatory deliverables.
  • Proficiency in R programming is a must.
  • Demonstrated experience with CDISC standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Proven ability to independently lead complex programming efforts across studies.
  • Experience mentoring staff and driving technical standards or best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently coordinate biostatistical projects, including planning and oversight of programming activities, with minimal direction from senior leadership.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS:

USD $131,100.00 - USD $160,000.00 /Yr.

EEOC Statement

WCG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer – Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment based on merit and without regard to race, color, national origin or ancestry, religion or creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression, gender identity, age, marital status, family or parental status, disability, genetic information, citizenship, veteran status, or any other legally recognized basis or status protected by federal, state, or local law. WCG complies with the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Act and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act. We promote a "One WCG" culture where all are welcome, respected, valued, and empowered to make a difference every day to advance clinical research.

Redwood Automation Solution Designer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance Close, Hungary

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Hungary. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

About Yadimen

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP finance close automation people in front of the client.

raw.description:
Encoded Therapeutics Inc. is a biotechnology company advancing precision medicines for a broad range of genetic disorders. Our mission is to unlock new opportunities for viral gene therapy through genomics-driven discovery. We focus on delivering life-changing advances for individuals with genetic disorders not addressable with current approaches. For more information, please visit.

Position Details

Encoded is seeking an Associate Director, Development Program Manager to drive the cross-functional planning and execution of a development program within our AAV gene therapy platform, focused on central nervous system (CNS) indications. Reporting to the Director, Development Program Management, this role is for an experienced program management professional who combines strong organizational and project-management expertise with a solid understanding of the drug development process, ideally including gene therapy or other advanced modalities. The Associate Director will serve as the operational backbone for the program team, working closely with Research, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Patient Advocacy and Medical Affairs to ensure program timelines, budgets, risks, and deliverables stay aligned and on track, while partnering with and escalating to the Program Management Organization (PMO) Director on major risks, resourcing conflicts, and strategic trade-offs.

Responsibilities

Program Strategy & Core Team Leadership

  • Facilitate development and implementation of program strategy, ensuring alignment with company goals, timelines, and budgetary constraints
  • Organize Development Core Team activities that foster cross-functional collaboration, effective communication, and strategic discussion, ensuring all stakeholders are aligned on program objectives and milestones to aid decision-making
  • Ensure cross-functional teams are properly prepared for internal meetings, communications to management, and engagement with external partners
  • Partner with the Director of PMO to ensure portfolio and cross-program considerations alignment

Program Planning & Execution

  • Develop and maintain the integrated program plan, timeline, and budget across all functional areas (Research, Nonclinical, Clinical, Regulatory, CMC,Medical, Patient Advocacy, Commercial) for the assigned program
  • Track deliverables resulting from Core Team meetings, ensuring timelines are met and objectives are achieved
  • Identify program risks and dependencies early, and develop and track mitigation plans in partnership with functional leads, with particular attention to the specialized considerations of AAV gene therapy programs (e.g., viral vector supply timelines, long-term follow-up requirements, specialized dosing or delivery infrastructure for CNS administration)
  • Assist functional leads with implementing risk management strategies, proactively identifying and mitigating program risks and challenges
  • Support scenario planning and contingency planning for key program decision points (e.g., go/no-go milestones, regulatory interactions, data readouts)
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of program management processes, templates, and best practices across the organization

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as the primary point of integration across functional areas for the program, ensuring consistent communication of program status, risks, and decisions
  • Partner with functional leads to coordinate cross-functional projects related to CMC, Regulatory, Clinical, Medical, Patient Advocacy, and Nonclinical, providing support and guidance to achieve project goals
  • Facilitate internal communication to identify risks and mitigations, escalating unresolved issues to the Director PM as needed

Budget & Resource Management

  • Partner with Finance and functional leads on budget forecasting
  • Support resource planning and capacity analysis across functions to ensure the program is appropriately staffed

Communication & Reporting

  • Monitor and report program progress, providing regular updates to cross-functional teams, the PM Director , and other stakeholders, highlighting key achievements, challenges, and mitigation plans
  • Utilize formal communication protocols and tools, including dashboards, reports, and weekly/monthly updates, to support company and operational goals
  • Support maintenance of program documentation in alignment with internal quality and compliance standards

Job Information:

About Computrition


Computrition, Inc. is a leading provider of enterprise foodservice, nutrition management, and retail technology, trusted by hundreds of organizations across North America, including healthcare systems, military installations, correctional facilities, and higher education institutions. For more than 44 years, we’ve built technology in partnership with our customers, helping them improve operational efficiency, strengthen financial performance, and deliver better nutritional care.


We’re investing in the future of our platform by adopting modern technologies and working closely with customers to solve complex operational challenges. Our solutions have real-world impact by driving performance enhancement and show up directly in how hospitals, military installations, and other institutions operate every day.


Computrition offers the stability of an established industry leader and the momentum of a company accelerating growth through innovation. We invest in our people and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and professional growth where employees can make a meaningful impact. You’ll join experienced professionals who are passionate about solving meaningful problems and delivering measurable outcomes for customers.


With team members across the U.S. and Canada, and as part of a growing portfolio of technology companies owned by Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU.TO), we are well-positioned to continue advancing the future of foodservice and nutrition technology.


If you’re looking to build technology that makes a meaningful impact while growing your career with a stable, innovative company, we’d like to hear from you.


The role

VP, Marketing owns how Computrition is understood in the market and how that understanding turns into pipeline, revenue and retention. This is a player-coach role: you set direction and personally build a meaningful share of the work.


Reports to: President and CEO

Location: Fully remote, United States

Travel: Up to 25 percent: industry conferences, customer visits, company events


You will work hand in hand with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and you are expected to know our products well enough to demo them and explain their business impact to a buyer.


What you will deliver in your first 90 days

  • Baseline metrics: a marketing scorecard with current funnel performance and a first report of marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline
  • Team alignment: match each team member's strengths to our growth initiatives, so their skills are applied where they create the most impact
  • Spend review: a review of marketing vendors and tools, with savings identified
  • Agreed priorities: Marketing's priorities validated with each department leader

What you will deliver in your first 12 months

  • A marketing plan and scorecard: an annual plan and budget with an investment case per program, and a monthly scorecard tying marketing activity to pipeline, bookings and retention.
  • Attributed pipeline: agreed marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline targets with Sales, reported monthly from our marketing automation platform and Salesforce.
  • A refreshed brand and website: a brand refresh and a rebuilt website, delivered on time and on budget.
  • Sales-ready materials: a current, consistent library of product, ROI and competitive materials that Sales and Customer Success actually use.
  • Events with measured return: every major conference run against meeting, pipeline and cost targets, with a post-event ROI report.
  • Customer proof: at least 10 quantified customer stories and an active reference program.
  • Higher output with AI: measurably more content and campaign throughput from the same team.

What you will own

Growth engine and measurement

  • Own Marketing's operating system: annual plan, budget, vendor management, and a weekly and monthly operating rhythm
  • Build and run the marketing scorecard, with leading and lagging KPIs and targets
  • Own attribution across our marketing automation platform and Salesforce, lead scoring, lead handoff to Sales, and data quality
  • Report Marketing's performance in executive and quarterly business reviews
  • Rationalize the marketing technology stack and vendor spend, and keep every marketing account and asset under company ownership
  • Agree Marketing's priorities and service levels with each department every quarter

Revenue support: new business and existing customers

  • Run campaigns and account-based programs that create qualified pipeline for new-business sales
  • Run expansion, adoption and retention programs with Customer Success for the installed base
  • Turn Product's value model into seller-ready business-case tools, and maintain a database of customer outcomes that proves value delivered
  • Maintain a proposal and RFP content library, including support for public-sector and government responses
  • Run win/loss analysis and feed the findings to Sales, Product and messaging

Product and sales marketing

  • Partner with Product on positioning, naming, packaging input and launch readiness for new products and releases
  • Produce and maintain product sheets, presentations, demo stories, case studies and competitive battlecards
  • Govern messaging so every customer-facing asset is consistent and current
  • Run co-marketing with technology and channel partners

Events: in person and virtual

  • Build the annual event calendar with an investment case and ROI target for each event
  • Run national and regional conferences end to end: pre-booked meetings, booth, customer receptions, follow-up and ROI reporting
  • Run webinars, virtual events and our customer user conference
  • Support internal company events, including our annual employee conference

Brand and communications

  • Lead the brand refresh and protect brand standards across every channel
  • Own social media strategy, PR, thought leadership, industry awards and customer recognition programs
  • Keep our external profiles (directories, analyst and data sites) accurate
  • Support employer branding and the careers page for recruiting

Website and digital

  • Lead the website refresh and own the site's performance: traffic, conversion and lead quality
  • Own SEO and visibility in AI search tools
  • Run the customer newsletter and email programs

Internal communications

  • Own the company intranet and its content
  • Produce the company-wide leadership newsletter and internal announcements
  • Run customer surveys through one tool and one intake process, so results are coordinated and acted on

Market sensing

  • Turn Product-led competitive and market insights into battlecards, messaging and sales enablement
  • Produce intelligence reports from every major conference
  • With Product and Sales, define ideal customer profiles and segments across healthcare, military, corrections and higher education
  • Bring the voice of the customer into product and pricing decisions

AI-enabled marketing

  • Lead AI adoption across the team: AI-first workflows for research, content, campaigns, personalization and reporting
  • Build and deploy practical AI tools and agents, including automation inside our marketing automation platform and CRM
  • Set quality, brand-safety and data-privacy standards for AI-generated content
  • Measure and report the productivity and performance gains AI delivers
  • Grow our visibility in AI search and answer engines

What you bring

  • 7+ years of B2B marketing in software or technology
  • Proof of delivered results: pipeline, revenue, conversion or retention gains you can quantify and attribute to your own work, and strategic initiatives you took from plan to completion
  • Demand generation and attribution: you have personally built demand programs and pipeline attribution in a marketing automation platform and Salesforce, or comparable platforms
  • Hands-on execution: you personally write, build campaigns, run the marketing automation platform and analyze the data, rather than only directing agencies or delegating
  • Decisiveness: you bring recommendations backed by numbers and own decisions within your authority
  • Deep product fluency: you have learned complex enterprise software well enough to demo it and model the ROI it creates for customers
  • AI literacy in practice: you use generative AI tools daily in production work, have built or deployed AI workflows or agents, and can show measurable gains in speed, quality or results
  • Transformation experience: you have led a brand refresh, a repositioning, a major launch or a rebuild of a marketing function
  • Event ROI: you have run conferences as measured investments, not just logistics
  • Tools: a marketing automation platform, Salesforce (or comparable CRM), a website CMS, web and campaign analytics
  • Remote collaboration: you drive cross-functional work effectively across locations and time zones

Preferred

  • Prior experience managing a marketing team
  • Experience marketing both on-premise and cloud software
  • Healthcare technology, healthcare foodservice or clinical nutrition background; a registered dietitian credential or close work with dietitians is a strong plus
  • Marketing to health systems, government or military buyers through long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles
  • Experience in a private equity-backed or holding-company software environment
  • Internal communications experience alongside external marketing

How to apply and compensation

With your resume, please include:

  • A one-page summary of two or three results you personally drove, with the numbers
  • One sample of work you created yourself (a campaign, page, deck or content piece)
  • A short description of an AI workflow you use in your marketing work today
  • After applying online, also send your resume, with attachments to

Finalists will prepare a marketing plan from a case study we provide, present it live, and meet with Product and Sales leaders.


Compensation: base salary of $115,000 to $140,000, depending on experience, plus an annual performance bonus and benefits. Final title depends on experience.

Computrition

Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain.

Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service.

Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees.

Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.

raw.description:
ABOUT STORD


Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.


By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.


With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.


Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like True Classic, Native, Seed Health, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

About the Role
The Regional Manager, Health, Safety, Compliance & Loss Prevention is responsible for executing and continuously improving Stord's HSS program across a defined region of fulfillment and warehouse facilities. Reporting to the Head of Health, Safety, and Security, this role translates enterprise standards into daily operational reality — driving consistent performance across sites, building regional team capability, and owning outcomes.

Regional Manager hires, develops, and directs a team of site-level safety and loss prevention professionals, holding them accountable to program standards while coaching them to grow. Success is measured by regional safety performance, loss prevention effectiveness, compliance posture, and the strength of the team built to sustain a culture.

What This Role Owns

Regional Managers are active partners in program design, governance, and policy-setting — contributing regional insight, operational context, and field intelligence to enterprise decisions led by the Head of HSS. They own translating those standards into consistent regional execution and are accountable for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that drive financial, operational, and asset loss across their region. The Regional Manager is accountable for:

  • Regional safety, compliance, and loss prevention performance metrics and trend improvement.
  • Translating enterprise standards into site-level execution — ensuring consistent, high-quality program delivery across every facility in the region.
  • Hiring, onboarding, and developing a regional team of HSS and loss prevention professionals.
  • Loss prevention strategy and shrink reduction for their region — including investigation oversight, security controls, and carrier/vendor accountability.
  • Regional compliance posture across OSHA, state regulations, and Stord internal standards.
  • Escalation management: serving as the regional decision-maker for incidents, investigations, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Risk ownership: proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across the region that could result in financial loss, operational disruption, or damage to people and assets — before they become incidents.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Development

  • Recruit, hire, and onboard site-level safety and loss prevention professionals within the region.
  • Set clear performance expectations, conduct regular coaching conversations, and deliver structured feedback and development plans.
  • Build a high-accountability, growth-oriented team culture within the regional HSS function.
  • Identify talent gaps and succession needs; develop internal candidates for expanded roles.
  • Facilitate regional team meetings, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving across sites.

Safety Program Execution

  • Deploy and sustain enterprise safety standards across all regional facilities, ensuring consistent implementation.
  • Conduct or oversee facility safety audits, gap assessments, and corrective action tracking.
  • Support site leaders and operations teams in embedding safety into daily standard work and leadership routines.
  • Lead or oversee incident investigations within the region, ensuring root cause analysis quality and timely corrective action closure.
  • Represent the region in enterprise safety forums, surfacing trends, risks, and improvement opportunities to the Head of HSS.
  • Coordinate peak readiness reviews to ensure safety standards are maintained through volume surges and labor onboarding.

Loss Prevention and Asset Protection

  • Own regional loss prevention strategy, including shrink reduction targets, security controls, and investigative outcomes.
  • Oversee internal investigations related to theft, fraud, and inventory discrepancy — escalating to HR, Legal, or Law Enforcement as appropriate.
  • Analyze loss trends across the region and drive root cause resolution through operational and procedural improvements.
  • Manage CCTV, access control, and physical security standards across regional sites, partnering with facilities teams on remediation.
  • Build relationships with carrier partners, vendors, and law enforcement contacts to support loss prevention outcomes.
  • Partner with Operations and Finance to quantify and report on shrink, damage, and loss impact at the regional level.

Compliance and Regulatory Management

  • Ensure all regional facilities maintain compliance with applicable OSHA, state, and local regulations.
  • Serve as the regional point of contact for regulatory inspections, responding to inquiries and coordinating any required corrective actions.
  • Monitor regulatory changes with regional applicability and coordinate with the Head of HSS to update procedures accordingly.
  • Oversee Hazmat compliance within the region, including proper storage, labeling, training, and incident reporting.
  • Support site-level readiness for customer-required certifications such as GMP, GDP, CTPAT, or TAPA where applicable within the region.

Metrics, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

  • Own regional safety and loss prevention KPIs, delivering regular performance reporting to the Head of HSS and regional operations leadership.
  • Drive trend analysis across regional sites to identify systemic risks before they become incidents.
  • Manage corrective action pipelines within the region, ensuring timely closure and verified effectiveness.
  • Champion near-miss and hazard reporting culture across sites, tracking participation rates as a leading indicator.
  • Partner with Ops Excellence to integrate safety and loss prevention improvements into standard operating procedures.

New Site Launches and Network Changes

  • Lead HSS readiness for new site launches within the region, including safety walkthroughs, program onboarding, and staff training.
  • Support automation and equipment commissioning activities from a safety perspective within the region.
  • Ensure staffing and program coverage scales appropriately as the regional network grows.

Required Qualifications

Experience

  • 7+ years of experience in health and safety, loss prevention, or operations compliance.
  • 3+ years of direct people management experience, with a track record of hiring and developing high-performing teams.
  • Multi-site experience in 3PL, eCommerce fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated experience in loss prevention investigation, shrink management, or asset protection in a high-volume logistics or retail environment.

Technical Knowledge

  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, state-specific safety regulations, and compliance program management.
  • Hands-on experience managing physical security systems, including CCTV, access control, and inventory protection protocols.
  • Familiarity with incident investigation methodologies and corrective action systems.
  • Comfort with Hazmat regulations and controlled substance handling requirements in a warehouse or fulfillment context.
  • Experience using safety and loss prevention data to drive operational decisions.

Credentials (Preferred)

  • ASP, CSP, or equivalent safety certification, or active pursuit of one.
  • Wicklander-Zulawski (WZ), Reid Technique, or equivalent interviewing certification preferred.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement background a plus.
  • Familiarity with CTPAT, TAPA, or SOC-related security requirements a plus.

Leadership Profile

  • A builder and developer of people — energized by growing a team, not just managing one.
  • Highly credible with frontline associates and site operations leaders; earns trust through presence and follow-through.
  • Capable of holding the line on standards while maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with operations partners.
  • Analytical and data-driven; able to translate metrics into clear narratives and actionable plans for regional and executive audiences.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity — able to triage competing priorities, escalate appropriately, and keep the team focused under pressure.
  • Strong written and verbal communicator; able to represent the region in enterprise forums and deliver clear guidance to site teams.

raw.description:
Nortek Data Center Cooling

Nortek Data Center Cooling builds the systems that keep modern data centers running — from liquid cooling to large‑scale air solutions. Our work supports some of the world’s most demanding AI and hyperscale environments, and we solve those challenges with engineering depth and practical execution.

We keep things simple here. We communicate early, stay close to the details, and follow through. When issues come up, we address them directly, not with layers of process. Customers count on us because we do what we say and we keep projects moving.


Our culture is hands‑on and collaborative. People take ownership, move quickly, and help each other. If you like working with teammates who are straightforward and accountable, you’ll feel at home.


With the backing of Madison Air, we have the scale, stability, and manufacturing footprint to support complex, high‑growth programs.

Nortek Data Center Cooling. is an equal employment opportunity employer and all qualiﬁed applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a qualiﬁed individual with a disability or any other characteristic protected by law.


Nortek Data Center Cooling offers comprehensive compensation and benefits package. Our benefits package includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life, STD, LTD, FSA, HAS and 401(k) Plan with company contributions. To apply, please visit our career site at .


Job Summary

The Metals & Fasteners Category Manager is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies across key direct material categories including carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, and industrial fasteners supporting Nortek Data Center Cooling's manufacturing operations. This role combines strategic category management with tactical execution, ensuring material availability, competitive cost structures, supplier performance, and supply chain continuity across multiple manufacturing locations.


The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of metals markets, fabrication processes, supplier management, and category strategy. This individual will leverage market intelligence, supplier partnerships, and cross-functional collaboration to drive cost reduction, support business growth, and ensure a resilient supply chain capable of supporting Nortek's expanding data center cooling business.

What You’ll Do

Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies for metals, fabricated components, and fastener categories.
  • Analyze commodity market trends, cost drivers, and industry indices, including CRU and other relevant market benchmarks, to support sourcing decisions and negotiations.
  • Build and maintain category strategies aligned with business objectives, supplier capabilities, and operational requirements.
  • Develop cost models, should-cost analyses, and forecasting tools to support procurement decisions.
  • Identify opportunities for cost reduction, supplier consolidation, and long-term value creation.
  • Manage the assigned category portfolio and maintain visibility to spend, pricing, and supplier performance metrics.

Supplier Identification & Management

  • Identify, evaluate, qualify, and develop strategic suppliers across metals fabrication, raw materials, and fastener categories.
  • Lead supplier negotiations covering pricing, lead times, service levels, inventory strategies, and capacity commitments.
  • Establish and maintain strong supplier relationships to ensure quality, delivery, responsiveness, and continuous improvement.
  • Monitor supplier performance using key performance indicators and implement corrective actions when necessary.
  • Evaluate supplier capacity and develop risk mitigation plans to support business continuity.
  • Support sourcing decisions related to direct-buy, distributor, and vendor-managed inventory (VMI) programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Design Optimization

  • Partner with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to support product cost, manufacturability, and supply continuity objectives.
  • Influence material selection and design-for-cost initiatives during new product development and product enhancement activities.
  • Recommend alternative materials, fabrication methods, and sourcing strategies that improve cost, quality, or lead time performance.
  • Support new supplier qualifications, product launches, and supplier transition projects.
  • Coordinate sourcing activities across multiple manufacturing locations to ensure alignment and standardization.

Supply Chain Execution & Operational Support

  • Collaborate with Planning, Operations, and Procurement teams to ensure material availability supports production schedules and customer commitments.
  • Manage supplier lead times, inventory strategies, and replenishment programs to balance supply continuity and working capital objectives.
  • Support multi-site inventory optimization initiatives.
  • Track, analyze, and report category spend, savings performance, supplier scorecards, and supply chain metrics.
  • Serve as a key escalation point for supplier-related delivery, capacity, and performance issues.

Risk Management, Compliance & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and maintain supplier risk assessments and contingency plans for critical materials and suppliers.
  • Ensure compliance with trade regulations, company sourcing policies, and applicable procurement standards.
  • Support sustainability, ethical sourcing, and supplier diversity initiatives where applicable.
  • Drive continuous improvement projects focused on cost reduction, supplier performance, inventory optimization, and process standardization.
  • Collaborate with Logistics, Quality, and Operations teams to strengthen end-to-end supply chain performance.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Materials Science, Operations Management, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of sourcing, procurement, or category management experience within a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Experience sourcing metals, fabricated components, industrial hardware, fasteners, or related direct material categories.
  • Strong understanding of commodity markets, metals pricing, fabrication processes, and cost drivers.
  • Experience developing category strategies, supplier negotiations, and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and collaborate effectively with technical teams.
  • Experience managing large SKU portfolios and complex supplier networks.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems, supplier performance management tools, and Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred

  • MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, or Business.
  • Experience sourcing across carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, and industrial fastener categories.
  • Familiarity with CRU indices, commodity forecasting, and should-cost modeling.
  • Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.
  • Knowledge of fabrication processes including laser cutting, punching, machining, welding, forming, and finishing.
  • Experience with supplier quality, global sourcing, trade compliance, and sustainability programs.
  • Background in HVAC, data center infrastructure, industrial equipment, or engineered products manufacturing.

Why Join Nortek DCC

  • Play an important role on a growing team
  • Contribute to a company helping power the next generation of AI‑ready data centers
  • Work in an environment with meaningful growth opportunities

Receptionist (Construction)

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a confident, organized, and customer-focused Remote Receptionist to support a construction business focused on roofing and custom home services.

This is a highly phone-based role combining inbound lead response, outbound follow-up, cold calling, appointment booking, and call tracking. You’ll be one of the first points of contact for potential customers, helping turn inquiries into booked consultations while ensuring every interaction is properly documented.

What You’ll Own

Inbound Lead Response

  • Receive and handle calls from leads who have submitted forms through the company website.
  • Qualify their interest and understand their needs.
  • Move qualified leads toward a booked appointment with the appropriate team member.

Outbound Lead Follow-Up

  • Proactively call prospects who have expressed interest but have not yet converted.
  • Keep the pipeline warm through consistent follow-up.
  • Reduce drop-off between initial inquiry and consultation.

Cold Calling

  • Conduct structured outbound cold calling campaigns.
  • Generate new interest in roofing and custom home services.
  • Follow established scripts while adapting naturally to live conversations.

Appointment Booking

  • Schedule consultations and site visits accurately.
  • Coordinate availability with the appropriate team members.
  • Avoid double-bookings and missed opportunities.

Call Tracking & Notes

  • Log every call, outcome, and follow-up action clearly.
  • Keep lead records accurate and up to date.
  • Ensure the team always has a current view of where each lead stands.

Professional Brand Representation

  • Serve as the first voice many customers hear.
  • Communicate warmly, clearly, and professionally.
  • Speak confidently about the company's roofing and custom home offerings.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Proven experience in a receptionist, call center, customer service, or inside sales role with a significant phone-based component.
  • Experience handling both inbound and outbound calls confidently.
  • Ability to conduct cold calls without heavy supervision.
  • Strong spoken and written English fluency.
  • Clear pronunciation and strong active listening skills.
  • Ability to keep callers engaged and conversations on track.
  • Comfortable using scheduling or CRM tools to log calls and manage appointments.
  • Specific platform experience is a plus.
  • Reliable home office setup with stable internet, a quality headset, and a quiet calling environment.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You remain calm and professional when calls become challenging.
  • You are comfortable handling rejection and staying consistent during cold calling.
  • You take ownership of lead follow-up rather than waiting to be reminded.
  • You proactively flag unusual or important customer situations to the internal team.
  • You are organized and consistently document every interaction.
  • You can work independently while maintaining close communication with the team.

What Success Looks Like

  • New website leads are contacted promptly and professionally.
  • Qualified prospects are effectively moved toward booked appointments.
  • Follow-up leads remain warm and receive consistent outreach.
  • Cold calling generates new conversations and interest.
  • Appointments are scheduled accurately without double-bookings or missed opportunities.
  • Every call and follow-up action is properly documented.
  • The team has a clear, up-to-date view of the lead pipeline.
  • Customers receive a professional and positive first impression of the company.

Typical Day

Your day revolves around the phone. You’ll start by reviewing new form submissions and prioritizing callback attempts for fresh leads.

As calls come in, you’ll qualify callers, answer basic questions about roofing projects and custom home builds, and schedule appointments on the calendar.

Between inbound calls, you’ll run outbound sessions, following up with leads that have gone cold and working through cold calling lists to open new conversations.

You’ll log every interaction as you go, ensuring the team has a live picture of the pipeline.

The role is largely independent, but you’ll stay in close communication with the internal team to flag hot leads, reschedule appointments, and surface anything that requires their attention.

Interview Process

  1. Recruiter Screening
  2. Client Interview
  3. Final Selection

About the role

Veradigm Payerpath is one of the most widely used revenue cycle and clearinghouse platforms in U.S. healthcare. More than 300,000 providers rely on us to check patient eligibility, submit clean claims, and track payments. We connect practices with payers, helping providers get paid faster and spend less time on paperwork.


We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead the Payerpath development team. You’ll manage 8–12 software engineers, own delivery of your teams’ outcomes, and keep a high-volume, business-critical platform reliable while continuing the team’s shift to AI-first development


What you’ll do

  • Lead AI-first development. Make AI a core part of how the team builds software. Put AI coding agents to work across design, coding, code review, testing, and documentation. Set the standards for using them safely with healthcare data, measure the gains in speed and quality, and coach every engineer to work this way.
  • Lead and grow the team. Hire, onboard, coach, and retain a team of software engineers who build, test, and support Payerpath. Raise the bar with every hire and development conversation. Set OKRs that tie to product and company goals, give regular feedback, and address performance issues promptly.
  • Own delivery and quality. Plan capacity across roadmap, maintenance, and support work. Keep commitments realistic and visible, and remove blockers so the team ships predictably. The team owns quality end to end: code review, automated testing, CI/CD, and secure development practices. Track delivery and quality metrics (throughput, defect rates, escaped defects, uptime) and use them to improve.
  • Keep the platform reliable. Payerpath moves high volumes of eligibility, claim, and remittance transactions for practices and payers every day. Partner with DevOps, Support, and Operations on production health, incident response, and root-cause fixes.
  • Work as one team with the business. Partner with Product Management, Architecture, Client Services, and Implementation to shape the roadmap, size work, and make sound trade-offs between new features, payer and regulatory changes, and technical debt. Focus on outcomes for customers, not activity.
  • Stay compliant. Make sure the team meets all regulatory and Veradigm security and audit standards.
  • Communicate. Keep the team informed on company and product direction, and keep leadership informed on progress against OKRs, risks, and staffing needs.

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 8+ years of software development experience, including at least 2–4 years managing engineers (direct reports, hiring, and performance management)-preferred.
  • Hands-on experience using AI development tools (such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or Cursor) and a track record of getting a team to adopt them.
  • A hands-on technical background with C#/.NET, SQL Server, and web services. You can review designs and code and guide technical decisions.
  • Experience running Agile/Scrum teams and delivering on a predictable cadence.
  • Experience supporting high-availability, transaction-heavy production systems.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and business audiences.

Nice to have

  • Experience working in a product operating model with empowered, outcome-focused product teams.
  • Healthcare revenue cycle, clearinghouse, or payer experience, including X12 EDI transactions.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA and healthcare data security requirements.
  • Experience with cloud platforms (Azure or AWS), containerization, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience working with distributed or offshore teams across time zones.
  • Experience building or shipping AI/ML features in a production product.

How we work

Our values shape how this team operates:

  • Unreasonably High Standards. Our clients and their patients depend on Veradigm. We set ambitious goals and raise the bar with every hire.
  • No Silos, No Handoffs. Engineering, Product, and Operations share ownership of the outcome.
  • Better Starts with Different. We question the status quo, and AI-first development is how we’re doing that today.
  • Outcomes that Matter. We work backwards from the customer and measure results, not activity.
  • Make Decisions AND Own Them. We decide in a timely way, commit fully, and stand behind the result.

Why Veradigm

Veradigm is a healthcare technology company that connects providers, payers, and life sciences organizations with data and solutions that improve care and lower costs. We offer competitive pay and benefits, including holidays, vacation, medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid life insurance, and retirement savings.

$113,254-$164,785

Compensation for this job is subject to market conditions, geographic considerations, the candidate’s unique skills and experience, state and local laws, and budget. Our commitment to pay transparency is a testament to our dedication to creating a fair, equitable, and inclusive workplace. By continuously analyzing market trends, staying abreast of changes in state laws, and making budgetary adjustments accordingly, we strive to ensure that our compensation practices reflect the value we place on our associates’ unique contributions and support their professional growth.


Enhancing Lives and Building Careers


Veradigm believes in empowering our associates with the tools and flexibility to bring the best version of themselves to work and to further their professional development. Together, we are In the Network. Interested in learning more?


Take a look at our Culture, Benefits, Early Talent Program, and Additional Openings.
